optimization_analysis: The original plan runs three sequential LLM calls per document: two SEM_FILTERs then a SEM_EXTRACT. The second SEM_FILTER (checking for residual clause and governing law) and the SEM_EXTRACT (pulling those exact fields) both read the same document sections and are semantically redundant — any document passing the second filter would immediately yield the extract. Fusing these two into a single SEM_EXTRACT that conditionally returns results only when both criteria are met eliminates one full LLM pass per candidate document while preserving correctness. The first SEM_FILTER is kept as a cheap, broad pre-filter to avoid running expensive extraction on clearly non-NDA documents.

optimized_semantic_plan.program:
SCAN_DOCS(CONTRACTEXHIBIT, all)
-> SEM_FILTER('Keep non-disclosure or confidentiality agreements', input_bindings={document: text})
-> SEM_EXTRACT('For agreements that contain a residual-information clause permitting use of information retained in unaided memory AND expressly state a governing law, return document_id, non_disclosure_direction, and governing_law; skip documents that do not satisfy both conditions', out_schema={document_id: string, non_disclosure_direction: string, governing_law: string}, input_bindings={document: text})
